bull_case: BTC at $63,813 (01:08 UTC July 6) — up +1.29% from Gate 2 confirmation close, 24h high $63,999 — means that Day 9 (July 6) opens into the strongest risk-on overnight tape of the entire distribution cycle. Bond distribution sellers are less motivated to aggressively press sell orders in a rising market environment. In the June 26 Russell 1000 inclusion context (Day 4), VIX was ~18 and the distribution was more aggressive. July 6 Day 9 opens with VIX 225bps lower — the marginal bond seller in a risk-on environment may wait for a better entry rather than selling aggressively into an upward market open. Best-case scenario: Day 9 comes in at 15–20M shares, significantly below the base case, pulling clearance forward to Day 11 (July 8).

VIX at 15.78 on Nasdaq 100 inclusion day (July 7, Day 10) is 225bps more constructive than the Russell 1000 June 26 inclusion day (VIX ~18). BTC at $63,813 adds the strongest crypto risk-on signal. The combination of maximum risk appetite (lowest VIX since pre-June) + maximum systematic demand ($4.3B passive) + minimum distribution remaining (est. 10–15M Day 10 residual) on the same day is unprecedented in the distribution cycle. If inclusion demand overwhelms Day 10 distribution, the close could print above $165–$170 — signaling that distribution is functionally complete a day early.

The triple holiday delay (July 3+4+5) has improved the IG floor buffer from $6.46 (July 2 session low vs $150 floor) to $12.00 ($162.00 reference vs $150 floor) without a single US market session. Three days of no negative SPCX news + BTC recovery from $57,802 (July 1 low) to $63,813 (July 6 morning) + NVDA recovery attempt ($194.83 AH after $200.06 peak) = the portfolio has improved materially during the holiday gap. The step-aside discipline preserved capital through the entire improvement.
bear_case: Day 7's non-monotonic volume spike (82.05M from Day 6's ~70M) showed that distribution can re-accelerate on any session. Day 9 (July 6) is the first US session after a 3-day holiday gap — sellers who couldn't distribute July 3 (abbreviated), July 4 (Saturday), or July 5 (Sunday) have 3 sessions of accumulated sell orders to release. Pent-up supply from a triple-closure gap could push Day 9 volume to 40–60M regardless of the BTC/macro backdrop — bond contractual distribution is independent of risk-on/risk-off conditions.

NVDA's evening OTC fade to $194.83 (from the morning's $197.16 and the day peak of $200.06) is a warning signal for the broader risk-on thesis. If the US chip sector that drove the $200.06 intraday OTC high could not hold above $195 on a Sunday with no institutional sellers present, the official July 6 open may see aggressive distribution from NVDA long positions — creating a risk-off environment for SPCX at exactly the moment when Day 9 bond distribution sellers are at maximum motivation.

Nasdaq 100 inclusion (Day 10, July 7) arrives while distribution sellers are still present at estimated 10–15M shares of residual volume. In the Russell 1000 June 26 template, QQQ/QQQM rebalancing demand was fully absorbed by distribution sellers same session. If July 7 mirrors June 26 (spike absorbed, close below Day 9 close), shorts who held through Day 10 are rewarded and the SPCX narrative reads as 'inclusion demand exhausted in 1 session.'

## Technical analysis (Sunday July 5, 2026 — end-of-day, 01:08 UTC July 6)

**No SPCX session.** US markets closed (Sunday). Last official close: $157.54 (July 2, Day 8). Reference: $162.00 (pre-market indication, unchanged).

**Step aside UNCHANGED. Updated framework summary:**
Bond distribution: Day 8 complete (~52M shares); Day 9 delayed three sessions (triple closure July 3+4+5); resumes July 6 at 9:30 AM ET (T-8H). Clearance est. Day 11–12 (July 8–9). Re-entry gate: $185 (two consecutive closes) after clearance. $162 reference is $23 (−12.7%) below re-entry gate.

**Overnight context — most constructive since IPO:**
BTC closed the July 5 UTC session at $63,813.77 (01:08 UTC July 6, Crypto.com MCP). 24h high $63,999. This is the most constructive overnight backdrop for Day 9 since the June 12 IPO — better than any single overnight session during the distribution cycle. Effect on Day 9: reduced marginal seller motivation → revised Day 9 estimate 15–30M (from 20–35M).

**IG floor buffer status:** $162.00 reference vs $150.00 floor = $12.00 buffer (unchanged). BTC's $63,813 close effectively eliminates the Korea-contagion IG floor risk that existed on July 2. July 6 opens with the most comfortable IG buffer since Day 5 of the distribution cycle.

**Triple holiday cumulative effect:** Three closure days have delayed Day 9 by 3 calendar days from original forecast (was projected for July 3 abbreviated). However, the delay has had two positive effects: (1) IG buffer improved from $6.46 (July 2 session low) to $12.00 (current reference); (2) Each delay day has seen BTC improve (July 1 $57,802 → July 5 close $63,813), creating a progressively better cross-asset backdrop for each successive Day 9 opening.

**Inclusion day (Day 10) context — VIX comparison:** July 7 Nasdaq 100 inclusion arrives with VIX ~15.78 vs June 26 Russell 1000 inclusion (Day 4) at VIX ~18. The 225bps lower VIX means risk appetite is higher, QQQ/QQQM systematic buyers are more aggressive, and the distribution sellers face greater institutional demand. The June 26 template (spike absorbed, close below open) remains base case, but the close-of-day price may be higher on July 7 than on June 26 in absolute terms.

**Key technical levels unchanged:** $185 re-entry gate. $150 IG floor. $162 reference in the distribution zone between $150 and $185.
